solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Around ten, sitting by wife, inspiring English philosopher (12)

indicatorNotes.by: by means beside, as in sitting by the fire, so W stands next to the jumble
indicatorNotes.inspiring: to inspire is to breathe in, so the jumble takes E inside

blocks.note: the letters of TEN SITTING jumbled
E = English, placed inside the jumble: ITTG(E)NSTEIN

annotation.surface: A scene of a family at dinner around ten o'clock, the wife beside someone.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma after 'ten' hides that TEN and SITTING are one pool of letters. 'Wife' reads as a person at the table; it is only W.
annotation.definitionFit: Ludwig Wittgenstein, the Austrian-born thinker who taught at Cambridge, is given by example of the class 'philosopher'.

entries.clue: Muffled music played originally during midweek (7)

indicatorNotes.originally: the origin of a word is its first letter
indicatorNotes.during: RAP and P fall within the middle of the week

blocks.note: WED, short for Wednesday, the middle of the week; it opens to hold the rest
rap is a genre of music

annotation.surface: Music heard through a wall, muted, in the middle of the week.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Midweek' is WED, the abbreviation for Wednesday, rather than a time. The surface wants 'Muffled' to describe the sound; it means bundled up.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of bundled up in scarves against the cold, not the sense of deadened sound the surface suggests.

entries.clue: Pull up boring character having a pair of shades (3-4)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down entry, up means read bottom to top
indicatorNotes.boring: to bore is to drill into, so WOT goes into TONE

blocks.note: tone = character, as in the tone of a place

annotation.surface: An instruction to stop a dull person in their tracks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boring character' looks like a dull person; 'boring' is the container signal and 'character' is TONE.
annotation.definitionFit: A descriptive paraphrase: a pair of shades is two colours, which is what the hyphenated adjective describes.

entries.clue: North of Paddington, maybe extremely grandiose development (9)

indicatorNotes.extremely: only the extremes, first and last letters, of 'grandiose'
indicatorNotes.North of: in a down entry, north of means placed above
indicatorNotes.maybe: Paddington is one example of a station

blocks.note: Paddington is a London railway station

annotation.surface: A grand building scheme planned just north of Paddington in London.
annotation.walkthrough: Paddington is one of London's main railway stations, and the surface reads like property news. 'Development' means growth in the womb, not a housing project.
annotation.definitionFit: A specific sense: the development of a baby in the womb, far from the building project the surface suggests.

entries.clue: Greek character, graduate touring one ancient Nile region (5)

indicatorNotes.touring: BA tours around I, surrounding it

annotation.surface: A Greek graduate on a trip round an ancient part of the Nile valley.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a sightseeing trip; 'touring' actually wraps BA around I.
annotation.definitionFit: Nubia was the ancient land along the Nile south of Egypt.

entries.clue: Residence ultimately built above eastern French city (7)

indicatorNotes.above: in a down entry, T and E sit on top of NANCY

blocks.note: Nancy, a city in north-eastern France

annotation.surface: A house finally built overlooking a city in the east of France.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Eastern French city' reads as one description, but 'eastern' is just E and Nancy stands alone.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: residence as the period of living somewhere, which for a renter is the lease they hold.

entries.clue: Forthcoming about supporting contest Neil regularly mounted (2,5)

indicatorNotes.regularly: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is taken
indicatorNotes.mounted: in a down entry, mounted means turned to read upwards
indicatorNotes.supporting: in a down entry, RE holds up the letters above it

blocks.note: even letters of cOnTeSt NeIl give OTSNI, then turned upwards

annotation.surface: A contest in which a man called Neil climbed onto a horse.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Neil regularly' tempts you to use only his name, but the regular letters run across 'contest Neil' together.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: what lies ahead of you, as in 'a treat in store', is what is coming.

entries.clue: Studio’s features possibly found in Daniel Radcliffe’s car? (7,6)

blocks.note: the studio is a pottery, and its features are the turning tables clay is thrown on

blocks.clueFragment: possibly found in Daniel Radcliffe’s car?
blocks.note: Daniel Radcliffe played the boy wizard in the film series, and a car runs on wheels

annotation.surface: A film star's car as a feature of a film studio.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Studio' suggests the film world, where Radcliffe works; the studio is a pottery. The question mark flags the joke: Radcliffe played Harry Potter, so his car has Potter's wheels.
annotation.definitionFit: A pottery studio is equipped with spinning wheels for throwing clay; the second sense is a pun on the actor's most famous role.

entries.clue: Secretly drunk (5,3,5)

blocks.note: as with a payment made out of sight, off the books
so drunk you have slid off your chair to the floor

annotation.surface: Someone who drinks on the quiet.
annotation.walkthrough: The two words read as one phrase about a secret drinker, but each is a separate meaning of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Two idioms: an under-the-table payment is covert, and a drinker who has sunk under the table is very drunk.

entries.clue: Huge claims backing course run for public speakers (7)

indicatorNotes.claims: to claim is to take hold of, so OS takes RATOR inside
indicatorNotes.backing: ROTA and R are read backwards

blocks.note: a rota is a set course of turns
R = run, as in cricket scoring

annotation.surface: Grand claims made in support of a course that runs for public speakers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Huge claims' looks like exaggeration; 'Huge' is OS and 'claims' holds the rest inside.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: orators are people who make speeches in public.

entries.clue: Meat’s first cut following bishop’s blessing (7)

indicatorNotes.first cut: the first letter of the meat is cut away
indicatorNotes.following: following means coming after, so ENISON is written after B

blocks.note: B = bishop, as in chess notation

annotation.surface: A bishop blessing the first slice of meat at a feast.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bishop’s blessing' reads as one phrase, but the bishop is only B and blessing is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An archaic synonym, the same Latin root as benediction, still met in poetry.

entries.clue: Pudding in a firm single mass brought over (7)

blocks.note: a pat is a small mass, as of butter

annotation.surface: A firm pudding served up as a single lump.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about a stodgy dessert; 'firm' is a company, not a texture. Tapioca is a milky pudding made from cassava starch.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this milk pudding of starchy pearls is one kind of pudding.

entries.clue: Vertebrate creature, tame one mostly I trained (7)

indicatorNotes.mostly: all but the last letter of ONE

annotation.surface: A tame animal that I trained myself.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a pet owner's boast; 'trained' is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Amniotes are the vertebrates whose embryos grow in an amnion: reptiles, birds and mammals.

entries.clue: Crest of bird, piece missing (5)

indicatorNotes.missing: PART is missing from the bird

blocks.note: the partridge is a game bird
a piece is a PART, and these are the letters that go

annotation.surface: A bird's crest with a bit of it gone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crest of bird' reads as a head feather; crest is a hilltop line instead.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the landscape sense: the crest of a hill is its top line.

entries.clue: Strong urge to travel in podiatrist’s case? (5,4)

blocks.note: an idiom for restlessness to be off somewhere
literally, an irritated pair a foot doctor might treat

annotation.surface: A foot doctor who longs to travel.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the literal reading: a podiatrist, a foot doctor, might well see a case of itchy feet.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom for wanderlust, and read literally a complaint a foot doctor treats.

entries.clue: Cry, react badly over upsetting rule squeezing university (9)

indicatorNotes.over: in a down entry, CATER goes over, above, the rest
indicatorNotes.upsetting: in a down entry, LAW is turned up, read bottom to top
indicatorNotes.squeezing: to squeeze something is to grip it tight on both sides, so WAL holds U within

annotation.surface: Someone overreacting to an unwelcome rule being forced on a university.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a campus protest; 'over' only places CATER above the rest.
annotation.definitionFit: A vivid synonym: a caterwaul is a shrill wailing cry, like a cat's at night.

entries.clue: Hunt down suspect possessing lead to intriguing mystery (9)

indicatorNotes.suspect: suspect letters are not to be trusted in their order
indicatorNotes.possessing: the jumble holds I among its letters

annotation.surface: A detective told to track down a suspect in a baffling case.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is itself a detective story: 'suspect' looks like a noun, a person to hunt, but is an adjective for jumbled letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A genre sense: mystery as a detective novel, of which the guess-the-killer story is the classic form.

entries.clue: Comparatively dull-witted Serb out rambling (7)

indicatorNotes.rambling: letters that ramble wander out of order

annotation.surface: A rather slow man from Serbia out on a country walk.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Out rambling' reads as a hike; 'out' is fodder and 'rambling' the jumble.
annotation.definitionFit: Obtuse means slow-witted, and obtuser is its comparative.

entries.clue: Fervent manner of female quitting work (7)

blocks.note: a thing's function is its work, what it does
F = female, and this is the letter that goes

annotation.surface: The passionate way a woman hands in her notice.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Work' is FUNCTION, as in what a thing does, not a job to quit.
annotation.definitionFit: A less common sense: unction, literally anointing, came to mean an earnest, fervent manner of speaking.

entries.clue: Joint festered after covering’s removed (5)

indicatorNotes.after covering’s removed: the outside letters, R and D, are taken off

blocks.note: the covering is the outer pair, R and D, and these are the letters that go

annotation.surface: A joint wound that went septic once the dressing came off.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a medical one, a wound festering under a bandage; the covering is the outer letters of RANKLED.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the ankle is one joint of the body.

entries.clue: Hurtful broadcast twin oddly put out (7)

indicatorNotes.put out: TI is put out of ADVERTISE

blocks.note: to broadcast is to advertise, spread word of
odd letters of tWiN, and these are the letters that go

annotation.surface: A cruel broadcast that upset a pair of twins.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put out' reads as upset, as though the twin were offended; it means removed.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: adverse effects or comments are harmful ones.

entries.clue: Revolutionary delicatessen keen to accommodate Middle-Eastern diet (7)

indicatorNotes.to accommodate: the two words hold the answer inside them

annotation.surface: A radical deli eager to cater for a Middle Eastern way of eating.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Diet' is not food but a parliament, as in the Diet of Japan.
annotation.definitionFit: A diet is a legislative assembly, and Israel's parliament is the Middle-Eastern example.

entries.clue: Persuades new Reform UK MP to interrupt opponents (7)

indicatorNotes.to interrupt: N and TICE break in between E and S

blocks.note: East and South, opponents at the bridge table
Richard Tice, a Reform UK MP

annotation.surface: A new Reform UK MP heckling rivals in the House of Commons.
annotation.walkthrough: Reform UK is a British political party and Richard Tice one of its MPs. In bridge, East and South sit as opponents.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: to entice is to persuade by offering a lure.

entries.clue: Follow on after Nottinghamshire’s No. 11, say, discontented umpire (5)

annotation.surface: A cricket scene: Nottinghamshire's last batsman at the crease and an unhappy umpire.
annotation.walkthrough: In cricket the No. 11 is the last batsman; here it means the eleventh letter. Nottinghamshire is an English county with a cricket team.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to segue is to follow on smoothly from one thing to the next.

entries.clue: Essentially grim struggle facing artist in warm coastal area (7)

indicatorNotes.facing: VIE faces RA, set beside it

blocks.note: the middle two letters of gRIm
to vie is to struggle, compete

annotation.surface: A struggling painter having a hard time on a sunny coast.
annotation.walkthrough: RA, a Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist.
annotation.definitionFit: A riviera is a warm, sunny coastline, like the French Riviera.

entries.clue: Permanent police trap in Californian city? (7)

blocks.note: a sting is a police set-up to catch criminals

annotation.surface: A long-running police undercover operation in a California city.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the order is reversed: the police trap sits after the city, making an LA sting.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: what lasts endures and so is permanent.

entries.clue: Can of Amarillo, so reasonable to purchase in retirement (7)

indicatorNotes.to purchase: to purchase is to take hold of, and these words grip the answer
indicatorNotes.in retirement: retiring means drawing back, so read backwards

annotation.surface: A pensioner in Amarillo, Texas finding something cheap to buy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb opening the sentence; it is the noun, a spray can.
annotation.definitionFit: An aerosol is a pressurised can that sprays its contents.

entries.clue: Consort quietly with criminal in bar, Lecter! (6,6)

blocks.note: the letters of IN BAR LECTER jumbled

annotation.surface: A warning to keep your voice down when drinking beside Hannibal Lecter.
annotation.walkthrough: Hannibal Lecter is the cannibal killer of The Silence of the Lambs, so 'criminal' seems to describe him; it signals the jumble.
annotation.definitionFit: Prince Albert was consort, the husband, of Queen Victoria.
